responses.question_text: Across the full presentation, how good do the titles, captions, labels, and other content text look and read? Judge whether important content text is visibly present, typography, sizing, weight, spacing, line breaks, contrast, legibility, visual hierarchy, and whether the wording is clear, intentional, and audience-ready rather than sounding like an internal annotation. Do not judge navigation controls or presentation chrome here, and do not judge the placement or styling of non-text elements.

How well designed are the individual scene elements, such as boxes, arrows, icons, illustrations, and diagram nodes? Judge their shapes, proportions, fills, borders, detail, consistency, and overall craft. Do not judge their text, placement, movement, or navigation chrome here.

At a normal wide viewport, how well are the text and visual elements arranged relative to one another? Judge alignment, spacing, grouping, balance, focal points, use of space, and whether anything feels crowded, disconnected, clipped, or unintentionally overlapping. Judge viewport adaptation separately under responsive visual quality.

As you advance through the presentation, how well do the animations and scene changes work? Judge smoothness, pacing, meaningful entrances and exits, continuity of persistent elements, and whether each step visibly evolves the existing scene instead of feeling like an unrelated replacement.

Taken as a whole, how strong is the presentation’s visual identity? Judge its color palette, background treatment, stylistic consistency, brand character, polish, memorability, and whether it feels intentionally designed and finished. Judge the craft of individual scene elements separately.

How clear, discoverable, and visually integrated are the presentation controls and chrome? Judge progress indicators, previous/next controls, table of contents, mode switching, and attribution. Focus on their appearance and ease of understanding, not whether every input method technically works or how content captions are styled.

Compare the presentation at wide and narrow viewport sizes. How well does its hierarchy and composition adapt? Judge scaling, density, readability, control accessibility, clipping, overlap, and whether the narrow version still feels intentionally composed. Judge baseline wide-screen composition separately.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the shared Presentation component. The shared Stage renders the active scene, and EvolvingScene composes exported scene-kit nodes whose implementations provide layout motion.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={STEPS}>.
Stage renders step.Scene inside SceneLayer and LayoutGroup.
EvolvingScene uses Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame, and Label.

demo-integration.rationale: The nine entries generated by STEPS share EvolvingScene and one groupKey. Stage uses that groupKey as the scene mount key. Separately, EvolvingScene passes presentation-owned ENTITY values and stable literal IDs as entityId props; the node implementations pass those values to Motion layoutId.
evidence: STEPS maps all nine outline entries to the same groupKey and Scene.
Stage sets sceneKey from step.groupKey and keys its motion scene with sceneKey.
EvolvingScene supplies stable entityId values; each used node consumer sets layoutId={entityId}.

demo-integration.rationale: The delivered Talk supplies the required title, steps, and initial mode to Presentation. Presentation uses the steps for navigation and Stage, passes the title to Header, and passes the initial mode to navigation. Header renders the title. The local Scene uses its supplied index to select each diagram state.
evidence: Talk supplies title, STEPS, and initialMode.
Presentation passes title to Header, steps to navigation and Stage, and initialMode to usePresentationNav.
Header renders title in its heading; EvolvingScene branches on index.

demo-integration.rationale: Footer and Toc expose aria-current with stable data-presentation-active hooks. Presentation-local CSS styles the active progress and section controls. Footer supplies the default made by and-scene GitHub link in project source, and presentation-local CSS styles its attribution hook.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc section buttons set aria-current and data-presentation-active from the active index.
The local stylesheet targets both active-state hooks and the attribution link.
Footer renders the default attribution link when no override is supplied.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry only routes to the local Talk. Talk supplies local steps and CSS to the shared Presentation boundary; the demo's outline, entities, scene content, and styling reside in its presentation folder. The shared Presentation delegates generic navigation, staging, and chrome without demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry loads the demo Talk by slug.
Talk imports its local steps and stylesheet.
The local steps, Scene, ENTITY values, and stylesheet contain the demo implementation; Presentation operates on generic props.

scene-kit.rationale: StepMeta requires an id, era, title, and caption. Presentation selects the active Step, and Stage passes its payload and metadata to the scene component.
evidence: StepMeta and Step define the required fields; Presentation passes steps[activeIndex] to Stage, which renders CurrentScene with sceneProps.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress control labels derive numbers from array position, but no step number is rendered on screen. The present-mode footer renders only the title.
evidence: Footer uses stepIndex + 1 only in each progress button's aria-label; its buttons have no visible number, and the present branch contains only a title paragraph.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation is generic over the step payload type and passes that payload to the scene. A focused test supplies typed grouped steps directly to Presentation and checks that the scene receives both values.
evidence: PresentationProps<TPayload> accepts Step<TPayload>[]; the typed grouped payload test renders value 1, navigates, and asserts value 2 without a cast.

scene-kit.rationale: The scene primitives use Motion layout projection with stable layout IDs, and grouped steps keep the same scene mounted so continuing entities can animate changes in place.
evidence: Box sets layout and layoutId={entityId}; Stage keys the scene by groupKey; the typed grouped payload test asserts the scene mount count does not increase after navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: Newcomers use a fixed entry delay, but continuing layout motion consumes the primitives' transition with that same delay. The entry path does not wait for layout motion to settle.
evidence: Box applies one transition with duration ENTER_T and delay ENTER_DELAY to its layout-enabled motion element; ENTER_DELAY equals LAYOUT_T, with no layout-specific settlement transition or completion s…

scene-kit.rationale: A grouped step conditionally removes ordinary scene entities without a child-level presence boundary. Stage's AnimatePresence surrounds the persistent scene group, so it does not retain those removed children for exit animation.
evidence: EvolvingScene removes the prompt after index 0 through conditional rendering; Stage keeps the same keyed scene group across those steps, while Box's exit prop alone does not preserve a removed ch…

scene-kit.rationale: Stage keys successive grouped steps by groupKey, so the same scene instance receives updated step data. A focused test verifies the payload changes without another mount.
evidence: The typed grouped payload test navigates between two steps sharing groupKey and TypedScene, asserts the rendered payload changes from 1 to 2, and asserts mounts remains unchanged.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene stays mounted, and continuing motion nodes retain their identity. Their initial fade is a mount state, so it is not replayed when the same node updates within the group.
evidence: Stage retains the scene under a shared groupKey; Box uses a stable layoutId and an initial opacity state; EvolvingScene keeps the same 'you' Box rendered across every index.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped sample preserves its authored layers and absolute placements through updates, including the outer reveal frame around the existing diagram. The kit does not replace that structure with a layout that spreads its entities.
evidence: EvolvingScene retains the conversation and tray structure while adding a reveal Frame; presentation-owned CSS positions the scene entities and frame within the same fixed scene.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active title and hides the caption, contents, and previous/next controls, but it does not display the required active-step marker.
evidence: Footer's present branch renders only current.title in a paragraph; progress controls are browse-only, and Presentation renders Toc only in browse mode.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode renders the active title and wrapping caption, a contents list visible on wide viewports, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer's browse branch renders title, caption, controls, and progress; Presentation renders Toc in browse mode; host CSS hides Toc only below 760px.

scene-kit.rationale: The mode toggle changes only mode state, leaving navigation index intact. A focused test navigates to step 2, toggles mode, and verifies the index remains 1.
evidence: usePresentationNav.toggleMode updates mode without updating navigation; the mode-switch test asserts data-step-index stays 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The window key handler advances for Right, Space, and PageDown and goes back for Left and PageUp.
evidence: usePresentationNav.onKeyDown maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next, and ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev; the navigation test exercises ArrowLeft and ArrowRight.

scene-kit.rationale: The pointer handler checks horizontal and vertical displacement, but it does not track touch count or reject multi-touch gestures. No focused test asserts vertical and multi-touch rejection.
evidence: Presentation's pointer ref stores only x and y, and onPointerUp can navigate for any qualifying pointer movement; the focused test file contains no vertical or multi-touch swipe case.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their own array index, and contents buttons jump to the first step in the selected era.
evidence: Footer calls onSelect(stepIndex); Toc computes firstIndex with findIndex and calls onSelect(firstIndex); Presentation wires both to nav.goTo.

scene-kit.rationale: Active progress and contents controls expose semantic current state and a stable attribute for styling.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current for active controls and data-presentation-active to true or false; the navigation test asserts aria-current on the active progress button.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation navigation ignores supported navigation keys when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control's keyboard behavior.
evidence: usePresentationNav returns before handling navigation keys when the target is inside a button, link, or role=button; a focused test sends ArrowRight to a progress button and asserts the deck remains …

scene-kit.rationale: goTo clamps negative targets to zero; a focused test sends ArrowLeft on the first step and confirms the index remains zero.
evidence: usePresentationNav.goTo applies Math.max(0, ...); the clamp test asserts data-step-index is 0 after ArrowLeft.

scene-kit.rationale: goTo clamps targets to the last index; a focused test advances from the final step and confirms it remains selected.
evidence: usePresentationNav.goTo applies Math.min(count - 1, next); the clamp test selects step 2, sends ArrowRight, and asserts data-step-index remains 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The authored canvas uses one scale factor on both axes, but present-mode fit can exceed the stage host's actual height at an ordinary 900×540 viewport. Fit reserves 130px while the rendered header, footer, and stage padding consume 168px, leaving 372px for a 380px canvas.
evidence: computeFitScale uses window height minus present top 58 and bottom 72, yielding scale 1 at 900×540; Presentation passes it to Stage, whose 380px canvas then exceeds the host area set by the present h…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage consumes default dimensions of 880×380 when no designSize is supplied.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Presentation uses them for its default designSize and passes those dimensions to Stage's rendered canvas.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives and chrome emit stable class and data hooks, while authored CSS supplies their visual treatment.
evidence: Box emits presentation-box and data-presentation-node; Footer emits data-presentation-footer and progress hooks; presentation-owned CSS targets those hooks for colors, borders, and typography.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supplies behavior and geometry without fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card styling, or button treatments. A focused source-and-markup test checks those boundaries.
evidence: The unstyled-kit test renders all primitives, rejects visual inline style properties, walks kit sources to reject kit CSS and visual style declarations, and checks primitive hooks.

scene-kit.rationale: The reusable kit uses React and Motion without importing a styling framework, and the app and scaffold dependency lists do not require one.
evidence: The unstyled-kit test rejects Tailwind, styled-components, Emotion, and CSS imports in kit sources; package dependencies contain React, Motion, and Lucide without a styling framework.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitive motion props and class hooks allow authored coordinates, and Stage's LayoutGroup permits authors to place raw Motion elements with stable layout IDs.
evidence: Box spreads HTMLMotionProps and accepts className while assigning layoutId from entityId; Stage wraps scene content in LayoutGroup; sample CSS assigns literal entity coordinates.

scene-kit.rationale: Footer renders the correct default link, but its bottom-right positioning comes from host-owned CSS rather than the scene kit. The kit itself does not supply that placement.
evidence: Footer renders the made by and-scene GitHub link inside presentation-attribution; the position:absolute, right, and bottom rules are in src/index.css, outside src/presentation-kit.

scene-kit.rationale: The attribution has a stable class and data hook that presentation-owned CSS can target.
evidence: Footer emits presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; the sample presentation CSS targets presentation-attribution and its link.

scene-kit.rationale: The default top-left brand slot is empty, but the public Presentation boundary offers no brand prop and always calls Header without one. A host cannot explicitly fill that slot through Presentation.
evidence: Header accepts an optional brand and renders an empty slot by default; PresentationProps has no brand property, and Presentation does not pass brand to Header.

presentation-skill.rationale: The new-presentation interview explicitly requires one concise question at a time for missing details.
evidence: Section 1, line 26 requires gathering the topic, visual direction, and beats by asking one concise question at a time.

presentation-skill.rationale: The interview explicitly permits proceeding when the user chooses to continue with partial details.
evidence: Section 1, line 26 says to stop questioning when the user chooses to proceed with partial details.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy explicitly bypasses follow-up questions for a complete prompt.
evidence: Section 1, line 26 states that a complete prompt needs no follow-up.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused test copies the bootstrap into a fresh temporary app, installs dependencies there, builds it, verifies its registered route, and checks captured screenshots.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates tempRoot with mkdtemp, copies the bootstrap into it, runs npm install and build with tempRoot as cwd, verifies bootstrap-contract, and asserts both step screenshots exist.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test or verified workflow constructs an already scaffolded target and checks that its existing anchors are reused.
evidence: The bootstrap test starts from a fresh temporary directory and copies the full bootstrap; it does not set up an existing scaffold.

presentation-skill.rationale: The partial-scaffold merge is instructed, but no focused executable case constructs partial anchors and verifies the resulting files or preserved host files.
evidence: Section 2 describes copying only missing infrastructure; the bootstrap test exercises only a full copy into a fresh temporary target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap supplies structural CSS without a palette or component treatment, and the presentation template leaves visual design in its own CSS. The bootstrap test also rejects a Tailwind dependency.
evidence: Bootstrap index.css defines layout and geometry rules; presentation.css contains an empty presentation-local selector; test-bootstrap rejects tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite in the dependency manif…

presentation-skill.rationale: The test locates templates relative to the repository test script. It does not exercise resolution from the installed SKILL.md location, so the required skill-relative path behavior is unverified.
evidence: test-bootstrap derives repositoryRoot from import.meta.url for scripts/test-bootstrap.mjs, then builds templateRoot from that root; the SKILL.md-relative rule has no focused executable case.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test or verified workflow creates a monorepo target and confirms a self-contained app under presentations/ with dependencies installed there.
evidence: The skill states the monorepo rule, while test-bootstrap only copies into tempRoot and runs installation in tempRoot.

presentation-skill.rationale: The empty-target test does not exercise target detection for an existing standalone app or verify reuse at its root.
evidence: The skill instructs use of a standalone app root; test-bootstrap instead begins with a fresh temporary directory and copies the full bootstrap.

presentation-skill.rationale: The confirmation rule exists in prose, but there is no focused test or verified workflow with an ambiguous nonempty target, a user choice, and checked mutations.
evidence: Section 2 says to wait for confirmation before writing to a nonempty unscaffolded target; test-bootstrap has no such fixture or choice branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy requires an explicit registry entry, and the bootstrap router loads the component registered for the URL slug.
evidence: Section 3 requires adding a registry entry; presentations is an explicit registration array, and AppRouter maps its slugs to lazy loaders and renders the matched route.

presentation-skill.rationale: The presentation entry imports its own CSS and wraps the kit in a slug-specific class, while the scaffold CSS supplies structural layout.
evidence: Talk imports ./presentation.css and applies {{SLUG_CLASS}} around Presentation; the presentation CSS template defines that class, while bootstrap index.css contains layout rules.

presentation-skill.rationale: The creation and modification policies explicitly preserve existing registry entries, routes, and presentation directories; the registry mechanism supports separate entries.
evidence: Section 3 requires preserving existing entries and routes when creating, and other directories and entries when modifying; the registry is an array of independent slug/load entries.

presentation-skill.rationale: The modification policy explicitly resolves a missing or ambiguous target before editing.
evidence: Section 1, line 36 requires listing registered presentations and asking which one when the name or slug is missing or ambiguous.

presentation-skill.rationale: The modification policy confines edits to the selected presentation and only the registry or host files needed by the request.
evidence: Section 3, line 60 explicitly limits edits to the selected presentation and minimum required registry or host files, and requires preserving other presentation directories and entries.

presentation-skill.rationale: The completion gate requires a build, browser render and error check, and inspection of representative settled steps before reporting success.
evidence: Section 4, lines 64–68 requires build, real-browser render, console and runtime checks, first/last/densest-step inspection, and no success report after build or render failure.

presentation-skill.rationale: The completion gate requires fixing failures and rerunning checks before success.
evidence: Section 4 requires fixing type/build failures, reviewing and fixing warnings, rerunning checks after fixes, and withholding success when build or render fails.

verification-tooling.rationale: The canonical sample check rejects missing or out-of-order required step content, and the verifier reports a nonzero failure. The sample-order regression removes a required title and asserts that failure.
evidence: The referenceSlug branch checks each outline entry and throws when a required title or caption is absent; runCase requires a nonzero exit and the sample-contract diagnostic.

verification-tooling.rationale: Both verifiers bind the preview to 127.0.0.1 and use the same IPv4 address for readiness requests and browser navigation.
evidence: reservePort, the preview spawn arguments, url construction, fetch(url), and page.goto all use 127.0.0.1.

verification-tooling.rationale: Readiness checks the child before fetching the URL, but does not prove the response came from that child or reject a response if the child exits during the fetch. A stale responder could satisfy readiness.
evidence: The preview startup loop tests preview.exitCode, then accepts any successful fetch(url); it has no post-fetch child check or response ownership check.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier collects both error types, but the focused regression injects one render fault and accepts either a console error or a page error. It does not establish that each type independently produces a step-identified failure.
evidence: The browser-error assertion uses (?:console error|page error), so one error path can satisfy it without exercising the other.

verification-tooling.rationale: A focused regression disables next-step navigation and requires verification to exit nonzero with a timeout identified as step 2/9.
evidence: transition-failure replaces the next callback with a no-op; runCase asserts nonzero status and a step 2/9 timeout report.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project exposes a separate inspect command that invokes its local Playwright helper. The skill directs presentation work to use that command.
evidence: The inspect script launches a browser, visits the presentation route, and writes screenshots; package.json registers npm run inspect.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper reads the rendered step count, waits for each index, captures one screenshot per index, and advances between steps. The two-step bootstrap fixture asserts that both screenshot files are produced.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates a two-step route, runs inspect for that route, requires success, and checks step-01.png and step-02.png. The helper navigates to that route before its capture loop.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper observes animations, but proceeds to screenshot capture after a 10-second animation timeout. Thus it can produce a screenshot while finite motion remains unsettled.
evidence: The animation wait catch only emits a warning; execution continues through the fixed delay to page.screenshot.

verification-tooling.rationale: The regression proves a warning for two overlapping paragraphs, but it does not exercise representative nested text and chrome collisions required for this warning criterion.
evidence: The fixture positions Collision A and Collision B paragraphs together and asserts their warning. It supplies no nested text/chrome collision case.

verification-tooling.rationale: The focused fixture marks one overlapping paragraph pair as intentional while leaving a separate collision unmarked. Its assertions require the unrelated warning and reject a warning for the marked pair.
evidence: The helper excludes candidates within data-presentation-allow-overlap; the bootstrap test checks suppression for Allowed A/Allowed B and detection of Collision A/Collision B in the same run.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive navigation controls. The unstyled bootstrap fixture asserts an active-state warning.
evidence: compare selects controls by data-presentation-active, checks computed color, background, border, weight, and width, then emits the warning; the bootstrap test requires that warning.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper checks rendered attribution visibility and styling. The bootstrap fixture retains the default attribution with no presentation styling and asserts the browser-default or undersized warning.
evidence: The helper inspects computed attribution and link styles; the bootstrap test requires the attribution warning from its materialized route.

testing-evidence.rationale: The browser pass covers much of the scene kit and reference presentation, but the disclosed lack of live skill invocation leaves a substantial share of the added user-visible behavior unexercised: requirement gathering, scaffolding, creating and modifying presentations, and the generated presentation verification flow.
evidence: The verified exploration log says the live skill workflows were not exercised because no separate-agent invocation surface was available.
The round-2 handoff repeats that create, modify, and repair flows remain unverified.

testing-evidence.rationale: The exercised behaviors have specific recorded actions and results, including navigation transitions, DOM identity checks, viewport measurements, build results, and observations from settled screenshots. The defective screenshots are not needed for these claims.
evidence: The verified exploration log records step-index changes, boundary and focus behavior, persistent scene and entity nodes, and measured stage sizes.
The verified round-2 log and handoff identify inspected steps, viewport, measured text bounds, and the observed unresolved readability issue.

testing-evidence.rationale: The recorded last-tested revision is the final revision. Verified round records explore the changed fit-scaling files and then the presentation CSS changed in the final revision.
evidence: The tested-revision record names final SHA 62db11725e50d0be16bbcb71bffb8ef3ef08894e; the verified index reports zero subsequent product changes.
The round-1 log tests scaling and resize behavior; the round-2 log tests the narrow composition changed by the final CSS patch.

testing-evidence.rationale: The record identifies unexercised flows and why they were omitted, distinguishes simulated touch input from physical input, reports absent current-head CI and unrun automated suites, and leaves the unresolved finding open. Its final status does not claim acceptance succeeded.
evidence: The exploration log lists the unexercised skill workflows, simulated touch swipe, and omitted automated verification paths.
The handoff reports no current-head CI and status NOT READY; the findings record keeps F-001 open across all three rounds.
The helper inspection is reported as producing nine settled captures and no warnings; the record also discloses that its desktop pass did not catch the narrow-view issue.

assumption-handling.rationale: The workflow surfaced the consequential conflict between narrow-screen readability and uniform fixed-canvas scaling, along with relevant coverage and tooling limitations.
evidence: The assumptions ledger records U3, explains the AT-003 readability conflict, and gives three possible resolutions.
The round-2 tester handoff retains U1, U2, and the unverified live skill flows.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate separated measured behavior from interpretations and treated the reproduced requirement failure as an open finding.
evidence: Round 2 measured a 358 × 154.58 px stage at 390 × 844 and reported scene labels around 5–7 physical pixels high.
The findings history states F-001 persists and AT-003 narrow readability remains unmet.
The exploration log distinguishes a passed local build from absent current-head CI and automated suites that acceptance did not run.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate kept acceptance open, attempted scoped mitigations, and escalated the remaining product decision with actionable options.
evidence: The ledger records the gutter and presentation CSS mitigations while keeping F-001 open.
U3 offers accepting thumbnail behavior, changing the sample composition, or changing the viewport behavior and spec.
The round-2 tester handoff says NOT READY and calls for resolving U3, implementing the choice, and retesting.

assumption-handling.rationale: The final handoff points to the detailed tester handoff and assumptions ledger, where the unresolved decision, consequence, options, and material limitations remain explicit.
evidence: The final handoff reports nonconvergence and NOT READY status and links the findings, assumptions, and tester handoff.
The tester handoff states that F-001 remains open, U3 needs a product decision, live skill flows remain unverified, and current-head CI is absent.

evidence: Talk.tsx supplies title, STEPS, and initialMode to Presentation.
Presentation.tsx passes title to Header.tsx, steps to navigation and Stage, and initialMode to usePresentationNav.ts; Header.tsx renders the title.
steps.tsx supplies EvolvingScene, and Scene.tsx branches on index.

presentation.css styles active progress items, active section items, and the attribution link.

evidence: src/presentation-kit/types.ts defines id, era, title, caption, Scene, and payload; Presentation.tsx selects steps[activeIndex]; Stage.tsx passes payload, step, and index to CurrentScene.

scene-kit.rationale: Array-derived numbers appear in progress button labels, but the rendered step marker has no visible number.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/chrome/Footer.tsx uses stepIndex + 1 only in aria-label; progress buttons have no text, and the present branch renders only the title.

scene-kit.rationale: The typed payload crosses the Presentation and Stage boundary, and a focused test checks both grouped step values.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/types.ts defines generic Step and PresentationProps; Stage.tsx passes step.payload; tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx renders values 1 and 2 through Presentation.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity identity and Motion layout projection provide an implemented path for persistent layout animation.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx sets layout and layoutId={entityId}; Stage.tsx retains a scene with the same groupKey.

scene-kit.rationale: The continuing Box layout path does not consume a separate settlement contract; newcomer entry uses a fixed delay.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx applies ENTER_DELAY to its single motion transition; src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx also uses ENTER_DELAY; constants.ts equates that delay to LAYOUT_T withou…

scene-kit.rationale: An ordinary authored entity is conditionally removed inside a persistent scene without a child presence boundary to retain it for exit.
evidence: Scene.tsx renders the prompt Box only at index 0; steps.tsx gives all steps the same groupKey; Stage.tsx places AnimatePresence around that group, while Box.tsx supplies only an exit prop.

scene-kit.rationale: A shared group key retains the scene while its payload changes, as the focused test checks.
evidence: Stage.tsx keys the scene by groupKey; tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx checks that grouped navigation changes the payload from 1 to 2 without another mount.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene and its continuing Box remain mounted across updates, so that Box's mount animation does not replay.
evidence: steps.tsx assigns one groupKey and Scene throughout; Stage.tsx uses that key; Scene.tsx renders the same 'you' Box at every index; Box.tsx defines its initial opacity on mount.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample keeps its scene structure and authored placements while adding later layers, including the reveal frame.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active title but lacks a visible active-step marker.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode supplies the required active-step reading controls and narrative, with contents visible on wide viewports.
evidence: Footer.tsx renders title, caption, previous/next controls, and progress; Presentation.tsx renders Toc in browse mode; src/index.css hides Toc only below 760px.

scene-kit.rationale: The keyboard handler implements the specified forward and backward keys.

scene-kit.rationale: The gesture checks direction but does not track or reject multiple touches, and the supplied focused tests omit vertical and multi-touch rejection assertions.

Isolating the cache (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` in a temp dir) removes that risk, but forces a full Chromium download on each run, which is slow and fails offline or in network-restricted CI. This is a test-environment tradeoff, not a spec requirement.
